papers.title: A multi-omics integration of bulk and single-cell transcriptomics identifies and validates a 16-gene epithelial-mesenchymal transition prognostic signature in tongue squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC) is a highly aggressive malignancy associated with unfavorable clinical outcomes, highlighting the critical need for dependable prognostic indicators. The epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a fundamental biological process driving cancer progression. This study aimed to develop and independently validate an EMT-associated gene expression signature for predicting prognosis in TSCC through a multi-omics strategy.
papers.summary: This study developed and validated a 16-gene prognostic signature based on epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) gene expression for tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC), using a multi-omics approach that integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomics. The signature was independently validated, offering a potentially reliable tool for predicting patient outcomes in this aggressive cancer.

papers.title: Tumor-hepatocyte crosstalk drives a hepatic lactate-TGF-β axis of CD8 + T cell exhaustion and immunotherapy resistance in small-cell lung cancer liver metastases.
papers.abstract: Liver metastases confer poor outcomes and attenuate the benefit of immunotherapy across solid tumors. This study investigated how the hepatic metastatic niche promotes CD8⁺ T cell dysfunction and immunotherapy resistance in small-cell lung cancer (SCLC).
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint identifies a mechanism by which liver metastases in small-cell lung cancer drive CD8+ T cell exhaustion and immunotherapy resistance: tumor cells communicate with hepatocytes to create a lactate-TGF-β axis that suppresses T cell function. The findings suggest that targeting this crosstalk could improve immunotherapy outcomes for patients with liver metastases.

papers.title: Scale-Aware Compositional Inference Improves Reproducibility and Uncovers Convergent Aging Programs in Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables analysis of molecular organization with anatomical context. Existing spatial differential expression methods are restricted to within-sample inference, forcing between-sample comparisons to rely on approaches adapted from single-cell RNA-seq. Here, we establish a scale-aware inference framework for spatial differential expression by modeling compositional constraints and variation in total RNA abundance rather than removing them through normalization, enabling calibrated between-sample inference at cell-level resolution. Our method produces more reliable results
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a new statistical framework for spatial differential expression that explicitly models compositional constraints and total RNA abundance variation, enabling calibrated comparisons between samples at cell-level resolution. The method improves reproducibility and uncovers convergent aging programs in spatial transcriptomics data, addressing a key limitation of existing approaches that are restricted to within-sample inference.

papers.title: SPAE: Deciphering Cell Cycle Dynamics and Cell States in Single-cell RNA-seq Data.
papers.abstract: Rapid advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology have enabled the investigation of gene expression changes at the single-cell level, particularly for elucidating the heterogeneity among cells and complex biological processes. This technique reveals subtle molecular differences within individual cells, thereby offering a unique viewpoint for the investigation of cell cycle progression, cellular differentiation, and disease pathogenesis. However, accurately identifying and analyzing cell cycle dynamics in scRNA-seq data remains challenging due to the complexity of the data and
papers.summary: The paper introduces SPAE, a new computational method for deciphering cell cycle dynamics and cell states from single-cell RNA-seq data. It addresses the challenge of accurately identifying cell cycle phases in complex scRNA-seq datasets, offering a tool to better understand cellular heterogeneity and biological processes.

papers.title: CellCover defines marker gene panels capturing developmental progression in neocortical neural stem cell identity.
papers.abstract: Defining cell classes is central to the analysis of growing single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlases. Marker genes are most often identified by differential expression (DE) methods that assess genes one at a time, ignoring the redundancy and complementarity revealed when genes are considered jointly. Working with binarized expression data, we instead seek discriminating panels of genes that together are specific to a cell type, framing marker-panel selection as a variant of the minimal set-covering problem in combinatorial optimization. This formulation efficiently searches the vast spac
papers.summary: CellCover is a new computational method that selects panels of marker genes for cell types by framing the problem as a minimal set-cover, rather than relying on one-at-a-time differential expression. This approach captures the combinatorial redundancy and complementarity of genes, and when applied to neocortical neural stem cell data, it identifies marker panels that better reflect developmental progression. The method offers a more efficient and biologically meaningful way to define cell classes from single-cell RNA-seq atlases.

papers.title: Cytoplasmic DNA Sensing Links LINE-1 Expression to Neuronal Senescence in Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence contributes to neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet brain-penetrant senotherapeutic strategies remain limited. Here, we identify long interspersed nuclear element 1 (LINE-1) retrotransposons as key regulators of neuronal senescence and the senescence-associated-secretory-phenotype (SASP) in AD. Using transdifferentiated induced neurons (iNs) that preserve donor-specific aging-associated molecular signatures, we show that pharmacological inhibition of LINE-1 with nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (nRTIs) or antisense oligonucleotides reduces p16 expre
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint identifies LINE-1 retrotransposon activation as a driver of neuronal senescence in Alzheimer's disease, linking cytoplasmic DNA sensing to the senescence-associated secretory phenotype. The authors show that inhibiting LINE-1 with nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors or antisense oligonucleotides reduces senescence markers in patient-derived neurons, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: An Integrated Transcriptional and Post-Transcriptional Regulatory Circuit Orchestrated by NUDT21 Maintains the Proliferation and Survival of Neuroblastoma.
papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most prevalent pediatric solid tumor, associated with a poor prognosis. While alternative polyadenylation (APA) is a key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism in many cancers, its role in NB remains largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study identifies NUDT21 as a key regulator of alternative polyadenylation in neuroblastoma, revealing an integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional circuit that maintains tumor cell proliferation and survival. The findings highlight APA as a critical mechanism in neuroblastoma pathogenesis and a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Pasta, a Versatile Transcriptomic Clock, Maps the Chemical and Genetic Determinants of Aging and Rejuvenation.
papers.abstract: With the growing burden of age-related diseases, understanding and modulating the aging process has become a priority. Transcriptomic aging clocks (TACs) can track biological age but remain limited by platform dependence, tissue specificity, or restricted accessibility. To address this, we developed Pasta, a robust and broadly applicable human TAC, built using a novel 'age-shift' learning framework. Pasta accurately predicted relative age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-Seq as well as microarray data. Its predictions aligned with senescent and stem-lik
papers.summary: The authors developed Pasta, a versatile transcriptomic aging clock that accurately predicts biological age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk, single-cell, and microarray data. Using a novel 'age-shift' learning framework, Pasta maps chemical and genetic determinants of aging and rejuvenation, offering a broadly applicable tool for aging research.

papers.title: GPSNorm: Gaussian Process Spatial Normalization for Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics technologies enable measurement of gene expression while preserving spatial tissue organization, but they remain highly sensitive to technical variability such as library size differences, slide-level effects, and spatial artifacts. Most existing normalization approaches treat normalization as a preprocessing step and perform downstream analyses on normalized values as fixed inputs, ignoring the uncertainty introduced during normalization. We introduce GPSNorm (Gaussian Process Spatial Normalization), a Bayesian spatial normalization framework that jointly models techni
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: GPSNorm is a new Bayesian normalization method for spatial transcriptomics that uses Gaussian processes to jointly model technical variability and spatial structure, accounting for uncertainty in normalization rather than treating it as a fixed preprocessing step. This approach improves downstream analyses by propagating normalization uncertainty and reducing artifacts like library size and slide-level effects.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell sequencing and machine learning to identify specific cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subsets and chronic inflammation as key drivers of poor outcomes in ovarian cancer, particularly after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The findings highlight potential targets for improving treatment response.

papers.title: Overactivation of SHH signaling induces a cascade of dedifferentiation and oncogenesis in a new mouse model for choroid plexus carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Choroid Plexus tumors constitute 10-20% of brain tumors in infancy. Among these, Choroid Plexus Carcinomas (CPC) are highly aggressive and result in poor survival. Details on tumor initiation and oncogenic events remain largely unknown, aside from a high prevalence of TP53 mutations and marked chromosomal instability. We generated hGFAP-cre::lsl-MYCN::lsl-Gli2(N)::Tp53fl/fl mice with recombination activity from embryonic day 13.5 onwards in CNS cells, leading to MYCN and Gli2 activation as well as TP53 inactivation. 84% of the mice developed ventricular tumors within 18 days of life, resemblin
papers.summary: This study introduces a new mouse model for choroid plexus carcinoma (CPC) by activating SHH signaling (via Gli2) along with MYCN overexpression and TP53 loss in CNS cells. The model recapitulates key features of human CPC, including ventricular tumors with high penetrance and early onset, providing a valuable tool to study tumor initiation and progression.

papers.title: Targeting a candidate stromal immune checkpoint: a cellular senescence signature identifies COMP⁺ cancer-associated fibroblasts associated with CD8⁺ T-cell exclusion via a predicted COMP-CD47 axis in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Resistance to immunotherapy in colorectal cancer (CRC) is closely linked to an immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment (TME), in which cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are key regulators. Cellular senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) are increasingly recognised as drivers of CAF activity, yet their systematic prognostic and immunomodulatory value in CRC remains poorly defined METHODS: Using transcriptomic and clinical data from the TCGA-COADREAD cohort, we screened differentially expressed cellular senescence-related genes (DE-CSRGs) and constructed a progn
papers.summary: This study identifies a cellular senescence signature in colorectal cancer that defines a subset of COMP⁺ cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) associated with CD8⁺ T-cell exclusion. The authors propose a predicted COMP-CD47 immune checkpoint axis as a potential mechanism and therapeutic target to overcome immunotherapy resistance.

papers.title: Cell-type-specific damage scores reveal kidney and liver disease trajectories in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Degenerative diseases progress through gradual cell-intrinsic damage that is difficult to resolve with bulk transcriptomics or discrete cell-state analysis. We introduce a generalizable single-cell and spatial transcriptomics framework that quantifies continuous damage trajectories in vivo using cell-type-specific scores. Applied to chronic kidney disease and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, the podocyte damage score (PDS) and hepatocyte damage score (HDS) place individual podocytes and hepatocytes on a health-to-damage axis. Across mouse and human single-cell RNA sequ
papers.summary: This paper introduces a generalizable computational framework that quantifies continuous cell-intrinsic damage trajectories from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data, using cell-type-specific scores. Applied to chronic kidney disease and metabolic liver disease, the framework places individual podocytes and hepatocytes on a health-to-damage axis, revealing disease progression across mouse and human samples.

papers.title: POSTN⁺ CAF-SPP1⁺ macrophage crosstalk is associated with immune exclusion and poor prognosis in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a highly lethal malignancy in which the tumor microenvironment (TME) plays an important role in disease progression and therapeutic resistance. However, the spatial organization and molecular basis of stromal-immune interactions in LUAD remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study investigates the spatial organization and molecular basis of stromal-immune interactions in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), identifying a specific crosstalk between POSTN⁺ cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and SPP1⁺ macrophages that is associated with immune exclusion and poor prognosis. The findings highlight a potential mechanism of therapeutic resistance and suggest new targets for improving immunotherapy outcomes.

papers.title: STWave: Fine-Scale Spatial Structure Discovery in Microscopic-Resolution Spatial Transcriptomics via Patchwise Wavelet Graphs.
papers.abstract: The advent of microscopic-resolution spatial transcriptomics ( μ ST  ) enables the mapping of tissue complexity at subcellular resolution. However, the massive increase in data volume introduces a critical "memory wall," significantly limiting the applicability of existing computational methods on deployable hardware platforms. In addition, traditional single-scale modeling approaches often struggle to disentangle weak biological signals from technical noise. To overcome these challenges, STWave is proposed as a scalable framework for spatial domain identification. Specifically, STWave first e
papers.summary: STWave is a new computational framework for analyzing microscopic-resolution spatial transcriptomics data, addressing the 'memory wall' problem and improving spatial domain identification by using patchwise wavelet graphs to separate weak biological signals from technical noise. It enables scalable analysis on standard hardware, overcoming limitations of existing methods for high-resolution spatial data.

papers.title: Modelling ischaemic AKI in human kidney organoids reveals injury-associated epithelial states and macrophage-epithelial crosstalk.
papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common clinical syndrome associated with high morbidity and progression to chronic kidney disease. Ischaemia is a leading cause of AKI, driving cellular stress, metabolic reprogramming, and injury-associated epithelial states. Scalable human models that enable controlled investigation of ischaemic injury, repair, and therapeutic targets in AKI remain limited. We therefore assessed the extent to which induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived human kidney organoids recapitulate key features of ischaemic AKI.
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that iPSC-derived human kidney organoids can model ischaemic acute kidney injury (AKI), recapitulating key injury-associated epithelial states and metabolic reprogramming. Using this model, the authors uncover macrophage-epithelial crosstalk that may drive injury and repair, providing a scalable platform for studying AKI mechanisms and testing therapeutic targets.

papers.title: A cross-vertebrate single-cell and spatial atlas reveals evolutionary trajectories of gastrointestinal cellular innovation.
papers.abstract: The cellular innovations underlying vertebrate gastrointestinal diversification remain largely unknown. Here, we constructed a single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlas comprising nearly 1 million cells from 10 species, spanning 500 million years of vertebrate evolution. Analysis of conserved gene co-expression modules shows that the repurposing of existing genetic programs, together with de novo gene emergence, drives cellular evolution. We link module remodeling to lineage-specific dynamics, including ciliated cell loss and the tuft cell emergence. Furthermore, we identify lymphoid aggreg
papers.summary: This study presents a large-scale single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlas of the gastrointestinal tract across 10 vertebrate species, revealing how cellular innovations arise through the repurposing of existing genetic programs and the emergence of new genes. It links specific cellular changes, such as the loss of ciliated cells and the emergence of tuft cells, to lineage-specific evolutionary dynamics.

papers.title: SPCC: Inferring Spatial Cell-Cell Interaction by Integrating Single-cell and Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Study of single-cell spatial biology reveals the importance of integrating single-cell and spatial data for capturing spatial structure at individual cell resolution in various fields. With the lack of cellular-level information in most spatial data, it is necessary to integrate single-cell and spatial data. Here, we developed a deep learning computational framework for alignment and mapping of unpaired single-cell and the spatial data by using adversarial joint-variational autoencoder and Random Forest model (SPCC). SPCC will generate a mapping matrix for single-cell and spatial positions tha
papers.summary: SPCC is a deep learning framework that integrates unpaired single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data to infer cell-cell interactions at spatial resolution. It uses an adversarial joint-variational autoencoder and Random Forest to map single cells to spatial positions, enabling the study of spatial biology at cellular level.

papers.title: Characterizing intra- and intertumor heterogeneity in ovarian high-grade serous carcinoma subtypes using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Ovarian high-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC) is an aggressive ovarian cancer with a heterogeneous tumor microenvironment (TME). Advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatially-resolved transcriptomics have enabled the study of complex TME. This study explores connections between molecular subtypes described from bulk transcriptomes and spatial domains characterized by distinct gene expression in HGSC and their variability between patients. We quantify both intra- and intertumor heterogeneity across 2D space and identify differing spatial patterns of gene expression pertaining to
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to characterize the tumor microenvironment of ovarian high-grade serous carcinoma, linking bulk molecular subtypes to spatial gene expression domains and revealing both intra- and intertumor heterogeneity across patients.

papers.title: A categorization of spatial transcriptomics methods for cell-cell communication analysis.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is involved in regulating cellular behavior in tissues. Spatial transcriptomics adds local context to gene expression, enabling more biologically grounded CCC inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone. Rapid method development has yielded diverse CCC methods, each addressing distinct biological questions through varied analytical frameworks. We review 33 recent methods and organize them into three categories: inference of communication networks at cell-type or single-cell resolution, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability and regulatory mod
papers.summary: This review categorizes 33 recent spatial transcriptomics methods for analyzing cell-cell communication, organizing them into three groups based on their analytical frameworks and biological questions. It provides a structured overview to help researchers select appropriate methods for studying tissue-level cellular interactions.

papers.title: Tumor-derived Parathyroid Hormone-Related Protein Is Associated with Suppression of Cytochrome P450 Expression: Evidence From Multimodal Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Cancer cachexia is frequently associated with altered pharmacokinetics and increased chemotherapy toxicity due to the downregulation of cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes. However, the molecular mechanisms driving this broad metabolic suppression remain poorly understood. This study investigated whether tumor-derived parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP) is associated with, and may contribute to, suppression of multiple CYP families. In a rat cachexia model, protein expression of CYP3A, CYP1A, CYP2C, CYP2D, and CYP2E1 was significantly downregulated in both the liver and small intestine. Cons
papers.summary: This study shows that tumor-derived parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP) is associated with the suppression of multiple cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes in the liver and small intestine, which may explain altered drug metabolism and increased chemotherapy toxicity in cancer cachexia. Using a rat cachexia model and multimodal transcriptomics, the authors provide evidence that PTHrP contributes to broad CYP downregulation, offering a potential mechanistic link and therapeutic target.

papers.title: Single cell CRISPR screen identifies antagonism between Nsd1-H3K36me2 and Ezh2-H3K27me3 orchestrates pluripotency transition.
papers.abstract: The transcriptional and epigenetic landscape imposes constraints on the self-renewal capacity and lineage specification potential of both naive and primed mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). CRISPR/Cas9-based functional screening coupled with single-cell RNA-seq (CROP-seq) establishes relationships between gRNA-mediated knockout genotype and transcriptome phenotype, providing a powerful tool to dissect gene regulatory networks. Here, we employed CROP-seq to investigate the epigenetic regulation governing the pluripotency network in mESCs. This highly sensitive method identified key genes essen
papers.summary: This study uses CROP-seq, a single-cell CRISPR screen, to identify epigenetic regulators essential for the naive-to-primed pluripotency transition in mouse embryonic stem cells. The screen reveals an antagonistic relationship between Nsd1-mediated H3K36me2 and Ezh2-mediated H3K27me3, which together orchestrate the transcriptional and epigenetic changes required for this transition.

papers.title: Transforming subcellular spatial transcriptomics: deep learning models for cell segmentation.
papers.abstract: Subcellular spatial transcriptomics (SSTs) is transforming biology by revealing where individual RNA molecules are located within intact tissues, providing unprecedented insight into how cells function and interact. Achieving this promise depends on accurately identifying the boundaries of individual cells, making cell segmentation one of the field's central computational challenges. A core methodological issue is how best to ensure correct and biologically accurate assignment of transcripts to cells using cell segmentation algorithms. Recent advances in deep learning models have been instrume
papers.summary: This review discusses the central computational challenge of cell segmentation in subcellular spatial transcriptomics (SSTs), emphasizing the need for accurate assignment of RNA molecules to cells. It highlights recent advances in deep learning models that are instrumental in improving segmentation accuracy and biological fidelity.

papers.title: The gut-immune-brain axis in CNS tumors: Causal roles of microbiota and inflammatory proteins unveiled by Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: There is a growing number of research suggesting that there is an association between gut microbiota and central nervous system (CNS) tumor. However, the causal relationships and the mediation effects of inflammatory proteins in the associations are unclear. We extracted genetic variants associated with gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and 4 subtypes of CNS tumors from published genome-wide association studies and performed a Mendelian randomization analysis to identify potential causal effects. The inverse variance weighted method was used as the main method. Mediation analysis and sing
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics to investigate causal links between gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and CNS tumors, identifying potential mediating roles of inflammatory proteins. The findings suggest specific microbial taxa and inflammatory pathways may influence CNS tumor risk, offering new insights into the gut-immune-brain axis.

papers.title: Developmental reversion underlies resistance to immune checkpoint blockade in kidney cancer.
papers.abstract: Despite the clinical success of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in the management of advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), many tumors develop acquired resistance, presumed to arise from a refractory subpopulation of persister cancer cells. Previous studies have provided insights into tumor microenvironment-specific drivers of ICI resistance in ccRCC. However, the extent to which ccRCC cells undergo phenotypic changes or selection under immune surveillance and ICI therapy remains obscure. To address this question, we assembled an atlas of ccRCC tumors combining single-cell RNA
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint investigates how clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) tumors develop resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). By assembling a single-cell atlas of ccRCC tumors, the authors find that resistant tumors undergo a developmental reversion, where cancer cells shift to a more primitive or progenitor-like state, which may underlie acquired resistance. This provides new insights into the phenotypic plasticity of ccRCC cells under immune therapy pressure.

papers.title: Multi-Modal Foundation Model with Whole-Slide Attention Enables Transferrable Digital Pathology at Single-Cell Resolution.
papers.abstract: Paired histopathology and spatial transcriptomics data are advancing our understanding of tissue biology and disease, but modeling both modalities at single-cell resolution while mapping local and distal cell-cell interdependencies remains computationally prohibitive. Here we introduce TissueFormer, a framework for pretraining foundation models with linear rather than quadratic computational complexity, overcoming a long-standing barrier to modeling long-range dependencies at scale. Trained on over 17 million image-expression pairs from 1.2K tissue slides, TissueFormer excels at predicting spa
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: TissueFormer is a new foundation model that integrates histopathology images with spatial transcriptomics data at single-cell resolution, using a linear-complexity attention mechanism to handle long-range dependencies across millions of cells. Trained on over 17 million image-expression pairs, it achieves state-of-the-art performance in predicting spatial gene expression and transferring across tissue types, overcoming computational barriers that previously limited such multi-modal modeling.

papers.title: VIDEO-Visual Integration of Drosophila Enhancer Organization: a tool for integrating and visualizing chromatin accessibility, in vivo transcription factor binding and motif occurrence in tissue-specific differentially expressed genes.
papers.abstract: Dissecting gene regulation today relies on many genomic assays-including transcriptional output from RNA-seq, chromatin accessibility from ATAC-seq, and transcription factor (TF) binding from ChIP-seq. Whereas numerous tools exist for each modality and some integrate data across modalities, few allow researchers to interactively explore and visualize how TF binding motifs intersect with transcriptional activity and chromatin accessibility in a tissue-specific context. Here we introduce VIDEO (Visual Integration of Drosophila Enhancer Organization), a web-based analysis tool that enables visual
papers.summary: VIDEO is a new web-based tool that integrates and visualizes chromatin accessibility, transcription factor binding, and motif occurrence in the context of tissue-specific gene expression in Drosophila. It allows researchers to interactively explore how TF binding motifs relate to transcriptional activity and chromatin state, filling a gap in existing genomic analysis tools.

papers.title: Progressive deterioration of adaptive immune repertoires in Down syndrome linked to interferon hyperactivity and lymphoid tissue disorganization.
papers.abstract: Persons with Down syndrome (DS), the genetic condition caused by trisomy 21 (T21), display strong dysregulation of adaptive immunity, which underlies high risk of complications from infections, widespread autoimmunity, and poor vaccine responses. However, the mechanisms by which T21 dysregulates adaptive immunity across the lifespan remain poorly understood. We report here a multimodal analysis of adaptive immunity across development and aging in DS, including deep B cell profiling by mass cytometry matched to transcriptome and proteome data, B and T cell receptor sequencing (BCR, TCR), and sp
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint reports a multimodal analysis of adaptive immune repertoires in individuals with Down syndrome across the lifespan, revealing progressive deterioration of B and T cell repertoires linked to interferon hyperactivity and disorganized lymphoid tissue. The findings provide mechanistic insight into how trisomy 21 drives immune dysregulation, which may explain the increased susceptibility to infections, autoimmunity, and poor vaccine responses in this population.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics analysis of osteoarthritis: pathway regulation, cell interaction networks, and therapeutic translation.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) transcends the outdated paradigm of mere "wear and tear" cartilage loss. It is now recognized as a complex, whole-organ disease driven by multifaceted interactions among diverse cell populations across synovium, cartilage, subchondral bone, and infrapatellar fat pad. The profound heterogeneity within these tissues and the spatiotemporal dynamics of pathological processes have, until recently, remained a "black box," limiting our understanding of disease initiation and progression. The convergence of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomic (ST) has
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent single-cell and spatial transcriptomics studies in osteoarthritis (OA), highlighting how these technologies have revealed the complex cell-type heterogeneity and intercellular communication networks across joint tissues. The authors discuss how this new molecular understanding is paving the way for targeted therapeutic strategies, moving beyond the traditional view of OA as simple cartilage wear-and-tear.

papers.title: ScanNet: Single-cell annotation informed by transcriptional regulation Network via iterative heterogeneous graph learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate annotation of cell types in single-cell transcriptome sequencing (scRNA-seq) data is critical for understanding cellular identities. The transcriptional regulatory networks (TRNs), which map the regulatory relationships between transcription factors (TFs) and their target genes (TGs), capture the molecular dependencies underlying transcriptional programs. However, most existing cell type annotation methods do not fully exploit this regulatory information. Therefore, we introduce ScanNet, a Single cell annotation method informed by transcriptional regulation Network, to integrate prior
papers.summary: ScanNet is a new computational method that improves cell type annotation in single-cell RNA sequencing data by integrating transcriptional regulatory network information. It uses an iterative heterogeneous graph learning approach to leverage regulatory relationships between transcription factors and target genes, leading to more accurate cell type identification compared to existing methods.

papers.title: Multiscale learning of gene network-driven phenotypic dynamics of single cells.
papers.abstract: Understanding how gene regulatory networks (GRNs) dynamically orchestrate cell fate emergence remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we present GRNvelo, a computational framework that reconstructs multiscale cell fate dynamics by integrating GRNs with phenotypic dynamics from temporal single-cell RNA-seq data. GRNvelo establishes a biologically interpretable and mathematically rigorous multiscale model that couples GRN-driven single-cell velocity with nonlocal cell growth-mediated population dynamics. To operationalize this model, GRNvelo devises a two-phase cooperative optimization algorithm
papers.summary: GRNvelo is a new computational framework that integrates gene regulatory networks with temporal single-cell RNA-seq data to model cell fate dynamics at multiple scales. It couples GRN-driven single-cell velocity with population-level growth dynamics using a two-phase optimization algorithm, providing a biologically interpretable and mathematically rigorous approach to understanding how gene networks orchestrate cell fate emergence.

papers.title: Ligand-based directed differentiation to produce granulosa-like cells expressing steroidogenic enzyme genes.
papers.abstract: The ovarian granulosa cells are responsible for producing hormones and supporting oocytes through maturation and meiotic resumption. There is a need to generate granulosa-like cells (GLCs) from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) to better model human gonadal development and to test the effects of exogenous or pharmaceutical compounds on the ovary. Here we report a rapid ligand-based protocol for differentiating hiPSCs into cells that express markers of the transient developmental lineages and steroidogenic pathway genes. Single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis identified can
papers.summary: This paper describes a rapid, ligand-based protocol for differentiating human induced pluripotent stem cells into granulosa-like cells that express steroidogenic enzyme genes, providing a new in vitro model for studying human ovarian development and testing pharmaceutical effects. Single-cell RNA-sequencing was used to characterize the differentiated cells, confirming expression of markers of transient developmental lineages and steroidogenic pathway genes.

papers.title: An end-to-end framework for single-cell-resolution, whole-transcriptomic spatial profiling in post-mortem human brain.
papers.abstract: Single-cell resolution spatial transcriptomics enables transcriptome-wide molecular profiling within intact tissue architecture, providing unprecedented opportunities to investigate cellular organization and disease-associated molecular states in the human brain. However, applying these technologies to post-mortem human brain tissue remains challenging due to RNA degradation, heterogeneity in tissue preservation, and a lack of standardized analytical workflows. These challenges are particularly pronounced for whole-transcriptome platforms, where successful implementation requires optimization
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint presents an end-to-end framework for performing single-cell-resolution, whole-transcriptomic spatial profiling on post-mortem human brain tissue, addressing challenges like RNA degradation and tissue heterogeneity. The framework includes optimized experimental protocols and standardized analytical workflows, enabling robust application of whole-transcriptome spatial platforms to archived brain samples.

papers.title: Identification and validation of circadian rhythm and astrocyte-associated diagnostic and therapeutic model for cirrhosis encephalopathy patients via integrative bioinformatic pipelines and in vitro validation.
papers.abstract: Cirrhosis encephalopathy (CE) is a severe neuropsychiatric complication of liver cirrhosis, characterized by cognitive decline. While circadian rhythm (CR) disruption and astrocyte dysfunction are independently implicated, their integrated role in CE pathogenesis remains elusive.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative bioinformatics and in vitro experiments to identify a diagnostic and therapeutic model for cirrhosis encephalopathy (CE) based on circadian rhythm and astrocyte-related genes. The authors validate the model's predictive power and demonstrate its potential for guiding treatment, highlighting the combined role of circadian disruption and astrocyte dysfunction in CE.

papers.title: Machine learning and single-cell RNA sequencing identify shared diagnostic genes and mechanistic links between antiphospholipid syndrome and carotid atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is an acquired autoimmune disorder characterized by recurrent vascular events in large, medium, or small vessels. These events contribute to cardiovascular disease primarily through thrombosis and atherosclerosis (AS). Carotid atherosclerosis (CAS) represents a particularly high-risk manifestation of subclinical AS in patients with APS. However, the shared molecular signatures linking APS and CAS remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning and single-cell RNA sequencing to identify shared diagnostic genes and mechanistic links between antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) and carotid atherosclerosis (CAS). The findings reveal common molecular signatures that may serve as diagnostic biomarkers and provide insights into the shared pathophysiology of these conditions.

papers.title: UNC93B1 drives IL-6/STAT3-dependent tumor-macrophage crosstalk and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Lipid metabolic reprogramming is increasingly recognized as a driver of breast cancer progression; however, how lipid metabolism-associated risk states are translated into immune remodeling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) remains unclear. This study aimed to identify a lipid metabolism-related regulator that mediates tumor-macrophage crosstalk and to experimentally define its role in breast cancer progression.
papers.summary: This study identifies UNC93B1 as a lipid metabolism-related regulator that promotes breast cancer progression by driving IL-6/STAT3-dependent crosstalk between tumor cells and macrophages, leading to epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). The findings link lipid metabolic reprogramming to immune remodeling and EMT, offering a potential therapeutic target for breast cancer.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell eQTL and multi-omics analyses reveal AIM1 and ANXA1 as immune-related hub genes and potential therapeutic targets in head and neck cancer.
papers.abstract: Head and neck cancer (HNC) is characterized by substantial immune heterogeneity and limited availability of clinically actionable molecular targets. Here, we developed an integrative single-cell eQTL-driven multi-omics framework to identify immune cell-specific causal genes and prioritize drug-repurposing candidates for HNC.
papers.summary: This study presents an integrative single-cell eQTL and multi-omics framework to identify immune-related causal genes in head and neck cancer (HNC), pinpointing AIM1 and ANXA1 as hub genes with potential as therapeutic targets. The approach offers a strategy for prioritizing drug-repurposing candidates by linking genetic variants to cell-type-specific immune gene expression.

papers.title: A multimodal analysis suggests partial IRF8/TLR7-associated myeloid transcriptional convergence between diabetic kidney disease and Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) affect different organs but share epidemiological associations and innate immune abnormalities. The extent and cellular basis of reproducible cross-disease transcriptomic convergence remain uncertain.
papers.summary: This study uses a multimodal analysis to investigate whether diabetic kidney disease (DKD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) share transcriptional signatures, despite affecting different organs. The findings suggest partial convergence in myeloid cells, potentially linked to IRF8 and TLR7 pathways, indicating a common innate immune component. This provides preliminary evidence for shared molecular mechanisms that could inform future therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Decoding the hypoxic injury landscape and hypoxic risk model construction in diabetic kidney disease: a multi-omics study.
papers.abstract: To identify the core hypoxic injury pattern of DKD, construct a DKD risk model based on hypoxic injury-related (HIR) score, and explore the potential therapeutic targets of DKD.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics data to characterize hypoxia-related injury in diabetic kidney disease (DKD) and builds a risk model based on a hypoxic injury-related (HIR) score. The model helps predict DKD risk and identifies potential therapeutic targets, offering new insights into the disease's molecular mechanisms.

papers.title: Beyond the hallmarks of cancer: enabling technologies reshaping cancer diagnosis, prevention, and treatment.
papers.abstract: Cancer biology has been organized for 2 decades by the hallmarks framework, articulated in 2000 and most recently revised in 2026. The pace of technological change in oncology now requires reframing how cancer is detected, prevented, and treated. This review argues that the hallmarks framework, while historically essential, is no longer sufficient on its own to capture contemporary cancer care, and repositions the discussion around enabling technologies that operate across and beyond individual hallmarks. papers.summary: This review argues that the traditional hallmarks of cancer framework, while historically important, is no longer sufficient to capture modern cancer care, and instead reframes the discussion around enabling technologies such as multi-omic liquid biopsy, AI-assisted radiomics, and digital pathology that operate across and beyond individual hallmarks. It highlights how these technologies are reshaping cancer diagnosis, prevention, and treatment.

papers.title: A tissue microenvironment analogous to certain tumor microenvironments facilitates HIV persistence.
papers.abstract: The HIV reservoir that establishes early upon infection and persists in tissues remains the primary barrier to a functional cure. While progress has been made to study the reservoir in blood compartments and specific cell types, knowledge gaps remain on the tissue microenvironment that facilitates persistence. The development of a novel immunoPET/CT-guided spatial transcriptomics pipeline has enabled the localization of foci of viral infection in tissues, rare events that are challenging to sample. Prior studies leveraging the pipeline have characterized the viral microenvironment (VME) gene s
papers.summary: This paper describes a tissue microenvironment that resembles certain tumor microenvironments and helps HIV persist in the body. Using a novel immunoPET/CT-guided spatial transcriptomics pipeline, the authors identified localized viral infection foci and characterized the gene expression profile of the viral microenvironment, revealing similarities to tumor-associated niches that support immune evasion and long-term survival.

papers.title: Precision Drug Delivery Strategies for Treatment-Resistant Depression: Opportunities and Challenges of FUS-BBBO and Spatial Molecular Profiling.
papers.abstract: In this review, treatment-resistant depression (TRD),a clinically defined subtype of major depressive disorder, is characterized by substantial disease burden and heterogeneous pathophysiology, with many patients showing inadequate or transient responses to currently available pharmacological therapies. Emerging evidence indicates that some treatment failures may reflect limitations in central nervous system (CNS) drug delivery in addition to disease heterogeneity and pharmacological factors. TRD treatment failure from a drug-delivery perspective is reviewed here, and barriers such as the prob
papers.summary: This review discusses treatment-resistant depression (TRD) from a drug-delivery perspective, highlighting that some treatment failures may be due to limitations in central nervous system drug delivery rather than just disease heterogeneity. It explores opportunities and challenges of using focused ultrasound-mediated blood-brain barrier opening (FUS-BBBO) combined with spatial molecular profiling to improve precision drug delivery for TRD.

papers.title: The spatial revolution in immuno-oncology: artificial intelligence decoding NK cell niches to predict therapeutic response.
papers.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are important effector cells of the innate immune system and have been investigated as a therapeutic platform for cancer immunotherapy. Although NK cell-based therapies have shown clinical activity in hematological malignancies, their application in solid tumors remains limited by restricted tumor infiltration, functional suppression, and the complexity of the tumor microenvironment (TME). Recent advances in spatial transcriptomics and artificial intelligence (AI) have provided new approaches for characterizing NK cell distribution, functional states, and cellular int
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial transcriptomics combined with artificial intelligence can decode the spatial organization and functional states of natural killer (NK) cells within the tumor microenvironment, offering new ways to predict therapeutic response in immuno-oncology. It highlights the potential of these technologies to overcome limitations of NK cell-based therapies in solid tumors by revealing the complexity of NK cell niches.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomic analysis identifies a necroptosis-prone thyroid follicular cell state in Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
papers.abstract: Hashimoto's Thyroiditis (HT) is the leading cause of primary hypothyroidism, characterized by progressive thyroid follicular cell (TFC) loss and diffuse lymphocytic infiltration. While apoptosis dominates TFC death in HT, the role of pro-inflammatory necroptosis in TFC destruction, especially its cellular heterogeneity, spatial distribution, and inflammatory microenvironmental regulation, remains incompletely elucidated.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to characterize thyroid follicular cells in Hashimoto's thyroiditis, identifying a specific cell state prone to necroptosis—a pro-inflammatory form of cell death. The findings reveal the spatial distribution and microenvironmental factors that may drive this necroptotic state, offering new insights into the mechanisms of thyroid follicular cell destruction beyond apoptosis.

papers.title: Tumor-neuronal hybrid programs reveal a spatially adaptive malignant state in glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) exhibits marked cellular plasticity, including partial acquisition of neuron-associated transcriptional features. We tested whether public GBM spatial and single-nucleus datasets reveal a tumor-neuronal program with spatial organization and distinction from canonical proneural-like identity.
papers.summary: This study analyzes public glioblastoma spatial and single-nucleus datasets to identify a tumor-neuronal transcriptional program that is spatially organized and distinct from the canonical proneural-like state. The findings suggest that GBM cells can partially adopt neuronal features in a spatially adaptive manner, highlighting a new axis of cellular plasticity in this aggressive brain tumor.
